stemMd: Which molecule has polar bonds but no net permanent dipole because of its symmetric linear shape?
explanationMd: Each carbon–oxygen bond is polar, but in linear carbon dioxide the two equal bond dipoles point in opposite directions. Their vector sum is zero. Bond polarity and molecular polarity must therefore be considered separately.

distractorRationale.c: Water is bent and has a net molecular dipole.
distractorRationale.d: Its single polar bond gives the diatomic molecule a dipole.
distractorRationale.a: Its pyramidal shape gives a net dipole.
distractorRationale.b: Its single polar bond is not cancelled by another.
